title: Core-periphery Models for Hypergraphs

problem.claim: Model and analyze core-periphery structure in hypergraphs.

contributions.claim: Introduces a random hypergraph model for core-periphery structure.
Develops scalable statistical inference and sampling algorithms using sufficient statistics.
Provides theoretical bounds on the size of the model-generated hypergraph core.

stated_novelty.claim: The statistical inference algorithm is described as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The inference algorithm learns embeddings corresponding to node reputation rankings within the hypergraph.
Experiments on hypergraphs with up to approximately 10^5 mined hyperedges report better fits than baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: Introduces a random model of hypergraph core-periphery structure.
Uses sufficient statistics to develop scalable inference and sampling algorithms.
The inference algorithm produces embeddings corresponding to node reputation rankings.
Derives bounds on the size of the generated hypergraph core.
Reports experiments on mined hypergraphs and comparisons with baselines.

source_observation.claim: The approach combines sufficient-statistics-based inference with a preprocessing step that is almost linear in the number of hyperedges.

interpretation.claim: Aligning computational structure with model statistics can support scalability on large relational data.

application.claim: When designing scalable hypergraph methods, identify sufficient statistics that enable near-linear preprocessing and inference.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish scalability beyond the stated runtime description or datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the model formulation or assumptions.
The abstract does not identify the baselines, datasets' exact sizes, or evaluation metrics.
The abstract does not provide details of the theoretical bounds or sampling algorithm.
